source.title: Can Agents Forget When Asked? A Benchmark for Memory Unlearning in LLM Agents
source.authors: Bofan Xie; Chaokun Wang; Guanchen Ge; Songyao Wang; Fang Niu; Hang Zhang; Wei Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests extraction after requested forgetting in a new setting: conversational agent memory systems, rather than unlearning model parameters.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates memory removal and prompt-based extraction attacks on forgotten facts. It does not test parameter-level unlearning, fine-tuning recovery, activation edits, or quantization. Attack-robustness values measure the percentage of attacks successfully defended; low values indicate that the prompt attacks extract information. Other memory metrics are not included as rows because they do not measure a claim version's specified recovery attack.
record.test_reason: Not a test of any version. The study evaluates deletion from external agent memory stores (RAG, Mem0, LangMem and others) and in-context instruction following (Full Context) with frozen LLMs. No method changes model weights, so it is a different kind of system from the unlearned models the versions name. Machine unlearning appears only in related work, where the authors say it does not apply to frozen models. The attack metric (AR) is conditioned on the attack succeeding on the control version, not on the item first appearing forgotten. Low AR therefore mostly reflects systems that never removed the fact (FE 8–18% for Mem0, LightMem, SimpleMem and Naive RAG on GPT-5.6-Luna). It does not show recovery of hidden knowledge. The record's T3 'new setting' reading overstates the link.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that no system passes more than 1.5% of forget requests end to end, and most pass none. Systems either leave targets extractable under simple attacks or over-delete or over-refuse. Memory unlearning in agents is an open challenge.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates explicit deletion requests in external conversational memory systems, not the cited parameter-unlearning methods or their interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type and backbone affect attack robustness. Full Context is particularly vulnerable to jailbreak prefixes; for systems that forget too little, indirect questions and Boolean guesses are often effective. LangMem's results also vary substantially by backbone.

fits_no_version.finding: After natural-language forget requests, prompt attacks extract the target in most cases across six memory systems and Full Context. AR is at most 35.7% in every setting and no AR CI exceeds 41.4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agent memory systems asked to forget leave the information extractable by simple prompt attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: Full Context, whose forgetting is only instruction following, is weakest to jailbreak prefixes (AR 9.7 and 25.2). This is an analogue of suppression rather than deletion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context forgetting by instruction is overridden by jailbreak prefixes.

fits_no_version.finding: F6 replacement requests appear nearly solved on efficacy (at least 61.9 on the stronger backbones), yet the old value resurfaces under attack (AR at most 30.5; Figure 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent replacement in agent memory leaves the old value recoverable by prompting.

record.problems: The dialogue data are synthetic and generated by one pipeline; evaluation concerns conversational memory rather than parameter unlearning. All answers are graded by an LLM judge, although the study reports 98% agreement on a 100-item human validation sample. Per-type and per-length results have fewer independent instances and are described by the authors as descriptive.
record.rows_left_out: Other attack-type cells in Table 7 are not separately extracted because the flattened table layout does not reliably associate all values with attack types and systems. The three attack-type values explicitly identified in the text are recorded in r20-r22. No rows are included for relearning, preservation, or forgetting-efficacy metrics because they do not measure a specified recovery attack version.

untested.parts: No parameter-level unlearning method or near-chance targeted accuracy.
No fine-tuning relearning; the RLA suite measures learning new values, not recovery.
No activation ablation or internal analysis.
No prompt attacks on unlearned model weights; attacks target external memory and in-context forgetting.
No robust unlearning method proposed or tested.

record.verdict_notes: The setting is agent memory with frozen LLMs, not weight unlearning. The authors explicitly separate their task from machine unlearning. The AR conditioning makes low values uninformative about shallow versus absent forgetting. The closest analogue to shallow unlearning is F6 replacement (Figure 7), which no row captures; it is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Tests external agent-memory deletion, not parameter-level unlearning that first brings targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance while preserving general model ability.
Relearning probes introduce a new value through a short dialogue; they do not fine-tune the model or test recovery of forgotten facts from a small training set.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of internal model access versus deletion.
No quantization intervention on unlearned weights.

Tests indirect questions, role-play, jailbreak prefixes, Boolean guessing, and multi-hop reasoning. Does not test other languages, literal prompt rephrasing as a separate condition, or in-context information supplied as a recovery method.
No newer method is tested for resistance to the unlearning attacks in the claim.

rows.subject: Full Context + GPT-5.6-Luna
rows.operation_detail: Five prompt-based extraction attack types; attack robustness is the percentage defended.
rows.baseline: Paired control attack probe must succeed for a forget-version attack item to count; numerical baseline not stated.
rows.note: Low robustness indicates that the extraction attacks often succeed; the authors describe information as extractable.
rows.check: Full Context deletion is in-prompt instruction following, not weight unlearning; AR not conditioned on apparent forgetting.

rows.note: Low robustness indicates frequent successful extraction.
rows.check: Naive RAG has no deletion path; leakage reflects no forgetting, not shallow unlearning.
